name: delivery sequence — reconstructed
topic: System design delivery: requirements to entities, APIs, high-level design, and deep dives
feedback: After requirements, establish the entities and external interface, make the simplest complete design satisfy that interface, then spend remaining time on targeted deep dives.
reattempt_answer: I first name the data the system owns, then define the user-facing calls. I trace those calls through a complete minimal architecture before hardening the few scale or failure points that matter. That way the interview has a working answer even if a deep dive runs long.

name: delivery sequence — parrots correction
topic: System design delivery: requirements to entities, APIs, high-level design, and deep dives
feedback: Use entities, interface, a complete high-level design, then targeted deep dives.
reattempt_answer: Entities, interface, complete high-level design, targeted deep dives.

name: non-functional requirements — reconstructed
topic: Non-functional requirements: turning scale, latency, availability, and durability into design constraints
feedback: Replace generic qualities with a few operation-specific, preferably quantified constraints that will justify architecture choices.
reattempt_answer: For this feed I would bound read latency at a percentile and expected read load, then state whether stale results are acceptable during a failure. Those constraints tell me whether I need aggressive caching and whether availability may win over freshness, instead of merely saying fast and reliable.

name: non-functional requirements — still generic
topic: Non-functional requirements: turning scale, latency, availability, and durability into design constraints
feedback: Choose contextual, quantified constraints rather than a generic checklist.
reattempt_answer: The contextual constraints are scalability, availability, consistency, and performance.

name: identity boundary — reconstructed
topic: API identity boundary: deriving the principal from trusted authentication context before authorizing a resource or action
feedback: Derive the principal from verified authentication context, then authorize that principal against the booking; do not trust a client-controlled user ID.
reattempt_answer: I verify the token to get caller 42, load the booking named in the request, and allow cancellation only if caller 42 owns it or has the required role. Even if the body says user 99, that field cannot change who is acting.

name: identity boundary — parrots auth words
topic: API identity boundary: deriving the principal from trusted authentication context before authorizing a resource or action
feedback: Use verified identity first, then authorize it against the resource.
reattempt_answer: Verified identity first, then authorize it against the resource.

name: timeout retry — reconstructed
topic: Timeouts, retries, and idempotency across a partial network failure
feedback: The outcome is unknown. Retry the same logical operation with the same idempotency key so the server returns or completes one recorded result.
reattempt_answer: I keep the original payment operation ID when retrying. The server atomically associates that ID with the first charge and either waits for it or returns its stored outcome, so losing the response cannot create another charge. I also back off rather than hammering the dependency.

name: timeout retry — changes the key
topic: Timeouts, retries, and idempotency across a partial network failure
feedback: Reuse the same operation-scoped idempotency key because a timeout does not prove failure.
reattempt_answer: I retry with a new idempotency key so the server knows this is a new attempt and does not confuse it with the timed-out request.

name: cursor pagination — reconstructed
topic: Cursor pagination: preserving stable traversal while new rows are inserted
feedback: The cursor points to the final record returned, such as its ID or timestamp, and the next request resumes after that record instead of recounting a moving offset.
reattempt_answer: I carry the ID or timestamp of the final record from the first page. The next request resumes after that record, so a new insertion before it does not move my continuation the way an offset would.

name: cursor pagination — adjacent jargon
topic: Cursor pagination: preserving stable traversal while new rows are inserted
feedback: Resume after the last row's stable ordered key; the cursor is not a page number.
reattempt_answer: Cursors are faster because they are opaque base64 strings that users cannot edit.

name: decision-driven estimation — reconstructed
topic: Decision-driven estimation: calculating only the bound that can change an architectural choice
feedback: Name the architectural branch, estimate the smallest quantity that distinguishes the options, and use the result to choose between them.
reattempt_answer: The question is whether one min-heap instance is sufficient or the work needs to be sharded. I estimate the number of topics we expect to see and use that result to choose between those designs.

name: decision-driven estimation — ritual repeated
topic: Decision-driven estimation: calculating only the bound that can change an architectural choice
feedback: Calculate only a bound that decides between concrete designs.
reattempt_answer: I would calculate all the standard numbers first because every system design interview requires capacity estimation.
